value.rationale: The natural initial condition of two unanimous opposed social camps yields a complete exact outcome distribution for all finite biclique sizes and heterogeneous activity rates, resolving which side eventually wins rather than merely whether the system converges. Equal-rate parity creates a group-size-independent even-camp advantage over odd groups and exact odd–odd neutrality; the (2,3) calibration requires reducing the advantaged side rate by a factor of two. These are structural finite-size sensitivity and tie-boundary results relevant for social influence, beyond generic numerical or textbook evaluation of a pre-given random-variable integral.
